summary: Nyanaponika Thera (1901–1994) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peradeniya and under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Mahasi Sayadaw. He founded the Buddhist Publication Society, serving as leader and editor (1958–1984) and president (~1958–1988).
Nyingcha Duoji works in Tibetology. He studied at Boston University and completed a PhD at Harvard University (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp and teacher Mark Elliott.
Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (1932–1999) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Kathok and Nyoshul monasteries and under teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Dilgo Khyentse, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Nyoten Jinbo (1880–1946) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under Baisen Azegami and held a professorship at Komazawa University.

Ogyen Trinley Dorje (born 1985) is active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, Tenzin Gyatso, Drub Pön Dechen Rinpoche, Dragpa Tenpa Yarpel, Bokar Rinpoche (~2000–2004), and Pema Donyo Nyinje.

Olaf Hansen (1902–1969) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937–1944), the University of Jena (~1944–1945), and the Free University of Berlin (~1950–1969).

Olav Hackstein (born 1962) specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Pennsylvania, Freiburg (Dr. phil. 1993), and Halle-Wittenberg (Habilitation 1999), later becoming full professor at the University of Munich in 2008.
Ole Holten Pind (1945–2018) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna in 2009 under the supervision of Ernst Steinkellner.

Oleg Grabar (1929–2011) specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Paris, Harvard, and Princeton (PhD ~1955), and held professorships at Michigan (1954–1969), Harvard (1969–1990), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1990–1998).

Oliver Codrington (1837–1921) was active in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Secretary of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and Honorary Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (attested 1892).

Oliver Hector de Alwis Wijesekera (1909–1990) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at University College, Colombo, and SOAS (PhD ~1936), later serving as Head of the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Ceylon (1943).
Oliver Philipp Frey works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna and held a post there.

Olivier Lacombe (1904–2001) specialized in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Faculty of Arts of Paris, where he held a post (~1959–1970) before joining Paris-Sorbonne University (~1970–1974).

Olle Qvarnström (born 1953) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the universities of Washington, Harvard, and Copenhagen, and under Tord Olsson; he held a post at Lund University (attested 2000–2005).

Om Prakash is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under Dasharatha Sharma, later teaching there, at Kirori Mal College (attested 1961), and at the Delhi School of Economics (attested 2003).

On Shionoya (1878–1962) was a Sinology scholar. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1902) and Leipzig University (~1906–1908), later holding a post at Tokyo Imperial University (~1920–1939).
Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Khenpo Shenga.

Orna Almogi specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and under supervisors David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts with the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project and the University of Hamburg (attested 2007).
